name: Juan Francisco Beckmann Vidal
name_chinese: 胡安·弗朗西斯科·贝克曼·维达尔
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Beckmann Vidal is chairman of Mexican tequila maker Jose Cuervo, which went public in February 2017 and raised more than $900 million.
Jose Cuervo owns Latin America's oldest active distillery, in the Mexican town of Tequila.
The company has been in the same family's ownership for 11 generations. Beckmann Vidal's son, Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta, serves as CEO.
forbes_facts: Known for its tequila, Jose Cuervo became a major producer of whiskey after it acquired Bushmills in 2015 for $719 million.
Jose Cuervo first exported its tequila to the United States in the 1800s. In 2015, the company generated 64% of its $18.7 billion sales in Canada and the U.S.

name: Zhou Bajin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025)
forbes_bio: Zhou Bajin and his daughter Zhou Xiaoping control Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems.
The duo cofounded the company in 1993; Xiaoping serves as its chairman and CEO.
Its customers include Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Geely and Nio.

name: Vinod Rai Gupta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2019); Hurun India (2016-2019)
forbes_bio: Vinod Rai Gupta draws her fortune from her holding in listed flagship Havells India.
The company, which is run by her son Anil, makes everything from electrical and lighting fixtures to fans, refrigerators and washing machines.
Havells was founded by Gupta's late husband Qimat Rai Gupta in 1958 as an electricals trading business.
The company has 15 factories and sells in more than 70 countries.
In 2024, Havells expanded its product range by launching built-in kitchen appliances such as cooking stoves and chimneys.
forbes_facts: The late founder bought the brand 'Havells' from a Delhi trader back in 1971.
The company's air conditioners called 'Grande', claim to cool down to 18 degrees centigrade in 45 seconds.

name: Tse Ping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Tse Ping is a member of the billionaire Chearavanont clan from Thailand and the guiding hand behind Hong Kong-listed Sino Biopharmaceutical.
He stepped down as chairman of Sino Biopharmaceutical in 2015 and ceded the role to his daughter Theresa, while staying on as senior vice chairman.
Ping's son Eric rose to CEO in 2022 and is the company's largest individual shareholder.
Trapped in China during the turbulent Mao-era Cultural Revolution, Tse was shipped off to the countryside from the southern city of Shantou and lost the opportunity to attend college.

name: Peter Beck
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Peter Beck is the founder and CEO of Rocket Lab, which develops and launches rockets, satellites and other spacecraft for government and commercial customers.
The New Zealand native founded Rocket Lab in 2006, moved its headquarters to California in 2013 and took it public via a SPAC merger that valued the company at $4.1 billion in 2021.
Beck owns nearly 10% of Rocket Lab, which generated $600 million of revenue in 2025 and is the third most frequent orbital launcher globally behind SpaceX and the Chinese government.
Rocket Lab, which is known for its smaller launch vehicles, plans to debut a larger rocket called Neutron in 2026, enabling the company to compete more directly with the giants of its industry.
A self-taught engineer, Beck skipped college in 1993 and built rockets in his spare time, while working for a decade at an appliance manufacturer and government research institute in New Zealand.

name: John Coates
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: John Coates is the co-CEO of U.K. company Bet365, one of the world's largest online gambling businesses.
He joined his billionaire sister and co-CEO, Denise, in 2001 to launch Bet365 after she sold some of their father's betting shops.
Bet365 has since become a global player, with over 53 million customers across 200 countries; John owns a quarter of the firm.
In July 2015, he became the vice chairman of English Premier League's Stoke City Football Club, in which Bet365 has a majority stake.
forbes_facts: Coates studied law at Bristol University and started his career as an attorney.
Bet365 handles more than $65 billion of bets a year.

name: Gabriele Gebauer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Gabriele Gebauer owns nearly 96% of Mewa, a full-service textile company, which she ran until 2014.
Mewa manufactures workwear and protective clothing and provides professional washing services.
The company clothes 1.1 million people with workwear across Europe and washes 1.2 billion cleaning fabrics annually.
Founded by her grandmother in 1908, today Mewa boasts 48 locations and employs about 6,000 people.
The company reached sales of $990 million in 2023.

name: Abdullah bin Sulaiman Al Rajhi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Abdullah bin Sulaiman Al Rajhi chairs Al Rahji Bank, which was cofounded in 1957 by his father Sulaiman and uncles Mohammed, Abdullah and Saleh.
For more than 35 years, he has held positions at Al Rajhi Bank, trades on the Saudi stock exchange and is one of the world's largest Islamic banks.
Al Rajhi Bank has $282 billion in assets and reports having more than 20.5 million customers.
Abdullah bin Sulaiman also chairs several other family companies, including Al Rajhi Capital and Al Rajhi Holding Group.

name: Ryan Horton
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Ryan Horton's late father Donald Horton (d. 2024) founded homebuilder D.R. Horton in 1978.
He inherited a share of the family's more than 10% stake in the business, which is America's largest builder.
D.R. Horton has built more than 1 million homes across 126 markets in 36 states. It did $36.8 billion in fiscal 2024 sales.

name: Koo Kwang-mo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Koo Kwang-mo is the chairman and chief executive of LG, one of South Korea's top five conglomerates.
He inherited shares of his late father and former LG chairman Koo Bon-Moo after his death in 2018.
He is an adopted son of the former chairman, who lost his biological son in 1994; Kwang-mo was born as a nephew to Bon-Moo.
In 2018, at age 40, he became the youngest chairman of a major Korean conglomerate.
LG has diversified into AI, biotech and cleantech.

name: Radha Vembu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun India (2017-2022)
forbes_bio: Radha Vembu gets her wealth from her stake in privately held Zoho Corp, which offers business software on the cloud.
The company was cofounded by her older brother Sridhar Vembu, who started the business initially as AdventNet in 1996.
A graduate in industrial management from the elite IIT Madras, Vembu is a product manager for email service, Zoho Mail.
Zoho's founder Sridhar Vembu stepped down as CEO in February 2025 taking on the role of chief scientist. His younger brother Mani is now CEO.
forbes_facts: Zoho is setting up a new campus which an house 2,000 people in the tier 3 city of Kumbakkonam in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu
Zoho is headquartered in both Austin, Texas and Chennai, India
Zoho was ranked #41 in the Forbes 2023 list of the top 100 privately held cloud computing companies in the world.

name: Kim Jung-woong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2020-2024); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Kim Jung-woong is the founder and chief executive of GP Club, a Seoul-based cosmetics firm.
His company is best known for its line of JM Solution facial masks, which have become a hit among Chinese consumers.
In 2018, Goldman Sachs invested 75 billion won ($67 million) for a 5% stake in the company. It reportedly exited the investment without a profit in 2022 due to declining sales at GP Club.
forbes_facts: Kim started his entrepreneurial journey selling video games and consoles from a small Seoul apartment.
After losing his father at age 15, Kim says he was driven by the need to make money early on.
